title: Steel for House Building: Buying, Checking and Accepting Rebar
desc: How to choose and buy rebar for a house, check its origin, store it on site and accept the reinforcement before pouring concrete, to avoid errors hard to fix.
summary: A guide for house owners on choosing, storing and accepting reinforcing steel for houses, with the current rules on construction material management.
body: p

Reinforcing steel determines the tensile and bending capacity of beams, slabs and columns. Poor-quality steel or steel placed contrary to the drawings is a defect “buried” in the concrete, very hard to detect and repair. This article helps owners control the steel from purchase to the concrete pour.
h2
1. Choosing and buying steel
ul
Buy the exact type, diameter and grade stated in the design drawings; do not switch to another type without asking the engineer.
Choose a supplier with a clear origin who provides invoices and the manufacturer's quality certificate for each batch.
Check that the identification marks on the bars (symbols, logo, diameter) match the documents.
Agree in the contract on quantity, type, technical requirements and the documents to be delivered.
p

Bar and coil steel are on the list of construction materials managed by the Ministry of Construction (Article 3 and Appendix I of Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD). The supplier must provide the buyer with certificates, certifications and related documents under the contract and the law; the contracting party checks the quantity, type and technical requirements before accepting the materials for use (Clauses 1 and 4, Article 14 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
h2
2. Storing steel on site
ul
Raise the steel off the ground and cover it from rain; do not leave it soaking in water or mud.
Stack each diameter separately to avoid taking the wrong one.
Lightly rusted steel can be cleaned; steel that is heavily rusted, flaking or reduced in section should be referred to the engineer before use.
h2
3. Accepting the reinforcement before pouring concrete
ol
Compare the quantity, diameter, and spacing of main bars and stirrups with the drawings for each member.
Check the position and length of laps and anchorages against the design; splices must not be concentrated at the same location unless the drawings allow it.
Check that spacers ensure the concrete cover; the steel must not touch the formwork.
The steel must be clean, tied firmly and not displaced; the top bars must not be trampled flat.

Prepare an acceptance record and photograph each area. The supervisor accepts within no more than 24 hours of receiving the contractor's request; if they do not agree, they must state the reasons in writing (Clause 3, Article 22 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
h2
4. Dangerous cost-cutting “tricks”
ul
Reducing the number of bars or the steel diameter compared with the drawings.
Replacing the correct type with cheap steel of unknown origin.
Omitting stirrups or widening stirrup spacing at column and beam ends.
Cutting slab or beam steel to pass electrical and plumbing pipes without asking the engineer.
p
These defects may not show immediately but they reduce the safety of the building. When you find them, ask the contractor to correct them before pouring concrete.
h2
5. Keep the records
p

Keep the invoices, quality certificates, acceptance records and photos of the reinforcement. They are the basis for warranty claims, for disputes, or when you later want to repair or add floors. note

This article is for reference; every building needs to be surveyed and designed by qualified professionals. The principles above do not replace the drawings, technical instructions and calculations of the structural engineer for each specific house.
